subject: Renewal discussion: Nebula Retail — committed capacity + SLA credit mechanics
messages:
From: Alex Hayes <alex.hayes@nebularetail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@nebularetail.com>
Date: Fri, 17 Mar 2028 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal: Nebula Retail - committed capacity + dedicated pilot

Soojin —

Thanks for the recent QBR. Procurement asked me to kick off a formal renewal conversation for our platform contract (current term expires 2028-05-31). A few high-level asks from our side:

- We want a 24-month renewal window with a capacity increase of ~45% (mainly generation tokens and a modest bump in embeddings).
- Nebula is very sensitive to price volatility — need a firm 12-month price-hold on the committed unit price.
- We’re open to a committed volume discount but need a way to protect against service regressions (latency/availability). Ideally, credits or fee offsets if latency SLOs slip.
- We’d like to trial Redwood Dedicated for one core workload (4-week pilot) as part of the renewal conversation — want the pilot metrics included in the renewal quote.

Attached: NR Renewal Requirements.xlsx (breakdown of peak windows and estimated token usage).

Can you share options (commit sizes, discount tiers, and an SLA-credit proposal) by next Wednesday? Legal will need a formal quote/term sheet to start redlines.

Best,
Alex
Alex Hayes
Head of Procurement, Nebula Retail
[Attachment: NR Renewal Requirements.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Hayes <alex.hayes@nebularetail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Mar 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Nebula Retail - committed capacity + dedicated pilot

Alex —

Appreciate the clear requirements and the spreadsheet — helpful. High level, we can structure three viable paths and include a 4-week Dedicated pilot metric appendix in the quote:

Option A (Conservative commit):
- 12-month committed token volume = current ARR * 1.25 (modest uplift)
- 8% committed discount on gen tokens; 12% on embeddings
- 12-month price-hold on committed unit price
- Burst pool available at 1.8x committed rate (paygo pricing)

Option B (Growth commit — recommended given your 45% target):
- 24-month committed volume = current ARR * 1.45
- 12% committed discount on gen tokens; 15% embeddings
- 12-month firm price-hold on the committed unit price (first 12 months of the 24-month term)
- One-time onboarding credit = $40k applied to first invoice

SLA / SLO credit mechanics (proposed):
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile token latency target = 350ms for standard routes.
- If 95th percentile latency exceeds target for a given calendar month, client receives a credit equal to 5% of that month’s committed invoice, up to a maximum of 2 months worth of invoice credits per contract year.
- Availability: >99.5% monthly availability target; breach triggers 10% credit for that month.

Pilot (Dedicated):
- 4-week pilot: we’ll instrument observability and produce a short report (latency at 95/99, throughput, and cost delta). If pilot meets mutually agreed performance gates, we include a one-time migration credit of $15k toward first-month Dedicated consumption.

Open items for your procurement/legal team to confirm: DOS for price-hold, acceptable credit cap ($X), and whether the onboarding credit should be amortized over invoices or applied upfront.

I’ve attached a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and a quote template — will convert to a formal quote once we align on the option.

Next step: If you’re comfortable, pick Option B in principle and I’ll ask our finance ops to prepare a formal quote + DocuSign.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Draft-MAP-v1.pdf]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Mar 2028 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Nebula Retail - committed capacity + dedicated pilot

Soojin — quick read-through: solid structure. Two internal notes:

1) SLA credit cap: suggest we cap annual credits at $25,000 for latency faults — keeps long-term exposure bounded while still meaningful for the customer.
2) For Dedicated pilot, include explicit rollback/fallback path in the MAP (if pilot shows >15% cost delta vs hosted, automatic right to back out to hosted with first-month credit applied).

I’ll backfill finance if Alex signals verbal approval for Option B.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Sr. Sales Operations Manager | Redwood Inference

From: Alex Hayes <alex.hayes@nebularetail.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Cruz <elena.cruz@nebularetail.com>, contract@nebularetail.com
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal: Nebula Retail - committed capacity + dedicated pilot

Soojin / Ben —

Thanks — Option B looks like the right path for us. A few confirmations before I ask Legal to proceed:

- Please set the annual credit cap to $25,000 as Ben suggested.
- Confirm that the 12-month price-hold applies to the committed unit price (we accept price adjustments on paygo/burst usage).
- Include the Dedicated pilot appendix and the rollback clause Ben suggested.
- Please send a formal quote + DocuSign link by Friday; procurement needs a signature window of two weeks to hit their fiscal quarter planning.

If you want, loop in Elena for contract points (cc’d).

Best,
Alex
Head of Procurement, Nebula Retail
